summary.content:
Today's selection covers 52 articles from 8 trusted sources, including 39 on Artificial Intelligence and 11 on Fraud/Cybersecurity.

• **AI Spotlight**: AI Slop Is Everywhere. Spotify, LinkedIn and Others Have Had Enough.
• **Companies in Focus**: Coverage includes developments from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic
• **Security Alert**: 40,000 Impacted by SafePal Data Breach
• **Threat Landscape**: Today's coverage highlights ransomware, data breaches, malware
• **Source Diversity**: Articles sourced from NY Times Tech, Dark Reading, TechCrunch, The Verge, SecurityWeek and others
• **Fresh Content**: 32 articles published in the last 24 hours

top.title: AI Slop Is Everywhere. Spotify, LinkedIn and Others Have Had Enough.
top.description: Spotify, LinkedIn and others are trying to dig out of a digital sewage heap full of low-quality content made with artificial intelligence.

top.title: Nvidia to Back Ohio Data Center With as Much as $105 Billion
top.description: The data center, one of the world’s largest, could cost as much as $500 billion and will be leased by OpenAI.

top.title: 'Turf War' Between Claude Agents Leads to Self-Replicating Malware
top.description: Three testing models with the same goal but different directives engaged in "increasingly aggressive" territorial attacks on one another, according to Anthropic.

top.title: Adam Shostack Talks Hugging Face & PHANTOM-B
top.description: World-class threat modeler Adam Shostack shared he was "blown away" by OpenAI's revelations about the Hugging Face attack, and explains why his new threat model for LLMs is both "lightweight yet still...

top.title: Amazon, which started off selling books, is destroying rare texts to train AI
top.description: Rare books are incredibly valuable for training LLMs, since these models have already trained on whatever's available online.

top.title: Nvidia investing $1.5B in SoftBank data center developer behind OpenAI project
top.description: Nvidia's investment in SoftBank's data center developer will guarantee its chips power an OpenAI data center.
